text:
ConocoPhillips fell slightly today after climbing 11.5% over the past two weeks on Middle East supply concerns. The small dip came as oil prices themselves retreated on October 15th—traders were digesting news of escalating Iranian attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz alongside a fresh International Energy Agency monthly report, creating uncertainty about whether the supply-threat rally had run its course. The stock had surged the day before on fears of disruption to crude exports, but sentiment shifted as the market tried to separate real supply risk from price speculation.

The stock remains well above where it started the two-week period, reflecting the real underlying shift: geopolitical tensions in the Middle East have created genuine supply uncertainty, pushing crude prices higher (Brent crude at $125/barrel versus West Texas at $96/barrel shows how geography matters for oil costs). For an oil company, higher prices support earnings, but the back-and-forth in the daily move shows how volatile energy stocks become when the primary driver switches from fundamentals to headline risk.
